newsitem.title: UK: NFC sells car leasing to GE.
newsitem.headline: NFC sells car leasing to GE.

text.p: British freight firm NFC Plc said it had agreed to sell its BRS car leasing business to U.S. group General Electric Co's GE Capital Fleet Services Ltd for 120 million stg cash.
NFC said contracts have been exchanged and it expects to complete the sale on July 5.

BRS Car Lease, which was developed out of NFC's in-house car fleet management operation, made an operating profit of 10 million stg in the year to end-September 1996 on net assets valued at 87 million stg.
"This disposal sharpens NFC's focus and liberates significant investment capacity for growth opportunities in our core logistics business," NFC chief executive Dr Gerry Murphy said in a statement.

The GE sale was announced on Wednesday as part of a wider round of disposals and rationalisation of non-core businesses, which also included disposal of its Lynx express parcels business to local management for 26 million stg.

It said it had also sold some businesses in the U.S. and Canada operated by its Pickfords removals division to Brambles. NFC said the BRS, Lynx and Brambles deals together were expected to yield net cash proceeds of 145 million stg in the current year and an exceptional profit of 20 million stg.

Murphy said the proceeds of the sales would be used to reduce group borrowings. Net debt at the end of March stood at 215.9 million stg, down from 240.1 million stg a year ago, to reduce gearing to 40 percent of net assets from 46 percent in March 1996.

Last year the company reported a sharp rise in profits in Murphy's first round of restructuring since becoming chief executive in 1995, with pretax profits rising to 105.2 million pounds for the year to September 30, up from 38.6 million pounds in 1994/95.
